01 // The setup03

Inception, but RFCs.

A technical talk started as a vulnerability deep dive. The better question was hiding underneath: why did the easy answer feel so complete?

  • The search result was fast.
  • The diagram was clean.
  • The citation trail changed the question.
  • The talk is born from preparing a more technical talk and noticing the research failure mode behind the examples.
  • The UAP platform-engineering lens matters here: unexplained signals are inputs to investigate, not conclusions to inherit.
  • Name the core tension early: polished summaries are useful, but they are not authority.

02 // Conflict rule05

When sources disagree, sort the room.

A clean answer can still crop out the research question. The source trail is how we find what got left out.

clear diagramvsthreat model

03 // Epistemology06

Some receipts weigh more.

01

Normative standards

RFCs, BCPs, standards-track drafts. Ultimate protocol authority and threat-model baseline.

02

Verification frameworks

OWASP ASVS, WSTG, cheat sheets. Turns consensus into testable requirements.

03

Vendor and maintainer docs

Specific implementation guidance. Valuable, but often optimized for adoption.

04

Conference research

Emerging attacks, edge cases, and practitioner context before standards catch up.

05

Tutorials and AI summaries

Orientation only. Useful entry points, not roots of trust.

  • Explain the hierarchy before any case study so examples do not hijack the talk.
  • The hierarchy decides how to arbitrate, not what to ignore.

04 // Case-file protocol07

Ask four small questions.

1

What does the surface answer say?

2

What do OWASP, RFC, ASVS, or the relevant authority say?

3

What is the load-bearing difference?

4

What does this force us to ask next?

  • These questions keep the security details in service of methodology.
  • The fourth question is the handoff from reading to engineering decision-making.

Case 01 // JWT storage09

Can script touch it?

The question is not whether the token is shaped correctly. It is who can reach bearer material after JavaScript is already running in the origin.

Starting pointStore the bearer token where browser JavaScript can read it
Source trailOAuth browser-app BCP + OWASP HTML5/ASVS storage guidance
Hidden assumptionJavaScript-accessible storage changes attacker capability
Decision testCan this architecture keep bearer material away from script?

A valid token in the wrong reachability zone is still an exposed credential.

  • Avoid teaching XSS mechanics. Use the storage conflict to teach claim tracing.
  • The phrase JavaScript-accessible storage is the kind of awkward sentence that does real security work.
LIVE SYSTEMDEFAULT // LOADED
  • Do not duplicate the baked-in line. Explain that defaults are not neutral; they encode priorities.
  • Use this to move from JWT storage into OAuth diagrams and source drift.
LIVE SYSTEMREADY
Case 02 // OAuth implicit11

The diagram is a fossil.

A professional vendor diagram can outlive the recommendation it came from. The research move is to trace the diagram back to the spec and then forward to the BCP that superseded it.

Starting pointA clean implicit-flow diagram in official docs
Source trailOAuth 2.0 Security BCP deprecates implicit for browser clients
Hidden assumptionDocumented does not mean recommended
Decision testWhich current flow matches the client threat model?

Documentation can preserve fossils. The hierarchy catches what the diagram cannot show.

  • Keep this focused on source drift: diagrams persist because docs are products too.
  • The point is not vendor-shaming; it is learning to check whether a recommendation has moved.

Case 03 // Password hashing13

Hashing is not one verb.

The surface answer says use SHA-256, or maybe bcrypt. The source trail asks for parameters, costs, attacker economics, and the reason memory-hard functions exist.

Starting pointUse a hash. Maybe salt it.
Source trailOWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet + Argon2id guidance
Hidden assumptionThe parameter table is part of the security claim
Decision testWhat cost can production tolerate and attackers hate?

The gap between hash and 19MB per guess is where the real decision lives.

  • Do not turn this into an Argon2 lecture. Show that standards include parameters and threat assumptions.
  • This is where defensibility requires numbers, not vibes.
LIVE SYSTEMMAP / TERRITORY
Interlude // representation failure14

The map is not the world.

Every abstraction bends perception. Research is how we find the residuals, the edge conditions, and the places where the map quietly edits reality.

  • Use the Matrix reference lightly: it reinforces model versus system without derailing the talk.
  • This sets up CORS, where the browser error becomes mistaken for the trust boundary.
LIVE SYSTEMREADY
Case 04 // CORS15

Working is not safe.

The quick fix is a permissive CORS header. The research move is to ask whether the response contains sensitive information and whether CORS is being mistaken for authorization.

Starting pointOpen the origin policy until the browser error disappears
Source trailOWASP WSTG cross-origin resource sharing tests
Hidden assumptionCORS is a browser trust boundary, not authorization
Decision testWhat data crosses origins, and who is allowed to read it?

Fixing a browser error is not proving a boundary.

  • Use this as the final methodology drill, not as a CORS primer.
  • The repeated pattern is now visible: surface answer, authority, omitted assumption, next question.

05 // Tooling17

Let it fetch, not decide.

Use it for

  • Orientation
  • Controlled-source summaries
  • Comparison matrices
  • Question generation
  • Outline cleanup

Do not use it for

  • Citations
  • Final authority
  • Current security guidance
  • Normative interpretation
  • Replacing the deep read

A concrete failure: ask for normative JWT storage guidance and the model may cite RFC 7519, which defines JWT structure but says nothing about storage.

  • This slide is deliberately pragmatic: AI is useful, but only when the source boundary is explicit.
  • The RFC 7519 miss proves the method should correct the speaker too.
LIVE SYSTEMUAP // HUMAN CONTEXT OFFLINE
06 // Maintainer context18

Find the person behind it.

Specs tell you what. Working groups, issue threads, changelogs, and conference talks often explain why the sentence had to be written that way.

  • Identify authors and working groups.
  • Read what changed across drafts.
  • Look for the sentence everyone argued about.
  • The circuit-board image is a deliberate human fingerprint inside technical infrastructure.
  • Use the UAP Platform Engineer identity as a quiet callback: anomalous signals become useful only after a human traces provenance and context.
  • This is where research becomes more than citation; it becomes context.
LIVE SYSTEMREADY
07 // Output19

Leave with a decision.

A bibliography is not enough. Good research produces a decision an architect can defend under scrutiny.

  • This is the take-home artifact. Every item turns research into a defensible engineering action.
  • Let the audience feel that the case studies were drills for this checklist.
